jobs.prompt:
TASK (roadmap R-028 'One board covers every machine': projects and orchestrators from the MacBook and the Mac mini appear on one board; each card shows its machine and swarm version; version drift is flagged). Tailnet only. This job writes a standalone module + CLI + test; another job wires it into the board server. Do NOT touch tools/swarm.mjs.

Context: tools/remote.mjs exposes a machine's board as https://<dns>:8443/ via `tailscale serve` (tailnet only, never Funnel); the board API is GET /api/board with the board token in header x-watch-token (tools/watch-server.mjs), returning { at, machine: {...}, projects: [...], server: { version, installedVersion, stale } , ... }. Machine identity locally: os.hostname(); version: versionInfo() in tools/server-version.mjs.

Write tools/board-peers.mjs (ESM, SPDX header):
- Peers file: `peersFile(env, home)` = env.SWARM_PEERS_FILE || ~/.project-swarm/peers.json. Shape { version: 1, peers: [ { name, url, token } ] }. Written atomically with mode 0o600 (tmp + rename, chmod 600). `listPeers()` never returns tokens to callers that print (export `publicPeers(list)` that strips token).
- URL rule `validPeerUrl(url)`: must parse; protocol https: with hostname ending in '.ts.net' (tailnet MagicDNS), OR protocol http: with hostname 127.0.0.1 or localhost (tests/local). Anything else is refused ('peer-url-not-tailnet'). Name /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,40}$/. Token /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,200}$/.
- CLI when run directly (`node tools/board-peers.mjs add NAME URL` reads the token from stdin, never argv; `remove NAME`; `list` prints names+urls only, never tokens): one JSON line, exit 0/1.
- `async fetchPeer(peer, { fetchImpl = globalThis.fetch, timeoutMs = 3000 })`: GET new URL('/api/board', peer.url) with header x-watch-token: token (never in the query string), AbortController timeout, `redirect: 'error'`; response must be JSON object with array projects; cap body at 5 MB. Returns { name, ok: true, at, machine: data.machine?.host ?? peer.name, version: data.server?.version ?? null, projects, orchestrators: data.machine?.orchestrator?.sessions ?? [] } or { name, ok:false, error: short text } (never throws, never echoes the token in errors).
- `createPeerCache({ ttlMs = 10000, fetchImpl, now })` -> { async all(peers) } returning cached results per peer, refreshing at most every ttlMs, fetching peers in parallel.
- `mergeMachines(local, remotes)` (pure): local = { name, version, projects, orchestrators }; returns { machines: [ { name, version, ok, error?, projectCount } ], projects: local.projects tagged machine/version + every ok remote's projects tagged { machine, version, remote: true } (a remote project whose id equals a local id keeps both, distinguished by machine), orchestrators tagged the same way, drift: { versions: distinct versions of ok machines sorted, drifted: versions.length > 1, newest } } and on every tagged card `versionDrift: true` when its version is not the newest.
Tests tests/board-peers.test.mjs (node:test, assert/strict, no network: a fake fetchImpl; temp peers file via SWARM_PEERS_FILE): URL rule (ts.net https ok; plain https elsewhere refused; http only for loopback); add/list/remove via the CLI with the token on stdin and the file mode 600, list never prints the token; fetchPeer sends the token only in the header, times out, handles non-JSON and redirects as errors without the token in the message; cache refreshes after ttl only; mergeMachines tags machine/version, flags drift on the older machine's cards, keeps same-id projects from two machines apart, and lists an unreachable peer as ok:false. Run `node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/board-peers.test.mjs` and `node tools/check-package.mjs`.

TASK: a read-only reader for the policy engine's auto-decisions ('Handled for you' on the board). The policy engine (branch feat/policy-engine-v2, tools/policy.mjs autoDecisionEvent) appends records shaped exactly { kind: 'auto-decision', at: ISO, rule, requestKind, requestId, project, machine, reason } to <project>/.swarm/orchestrator/events.ndjson, and (with `ts` instead of `at`) to <project>/.swarm/project/journal.ndjson. Note: tools/orchestrator-events.mjs readEvents drops these lines (they have `kind`, not `e`), so read the files raw. Do NOT touch tools/swarm.mjs or the orchestrator-events/journal modules.
Write tools/handled.mjs (ESM, SPDX header): `async handledForProject(root, { now = Date.now(), limit = 20 })` reads both files line by line (cap 2 MB tail of each file: read only the last 2 MB if larger; skip bad lines), keeps kind === 'auto-decision', normalizes at = at ?? ts, de-duplicates the same decision seen in both files (same at within 2 s, rule, requestKind, requestId), sanitizes strings (trim, max 120 chars, strip control chars), sorts newest first and returns { today: count with at on the same UTC day as now, week: count in the last 7 days, total, items: first `limit` items [{ at, rule, requestKind, requestId, reason, machine }], byRule: { rule: count today } }. Never throws (missing files -> zeros). Tests tests/handled.test.mjs (node:test, assert/strict, temp dirs): reads both files, de-dupes the journal/events twin, ignores other kinds and bad lines, counts today/week by UTC day, limit and newest-first order, missing files give zeros, long and control-char strings are cleaned. Run `node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/handled.test.mjs` and `node tools/check-package.mjs`.

TASK: find the Claude Code Remote Control URL for an orchestrator session so the board can show an 'Open chat' link on its card (roadmap R-029). Read-only. Do NOT touch tools/swarm.mjs.
Facts: Claude Code writes one file per live process at ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json with fields including pid, sessionId (the same id the orchestrator hook records as the session id), cwd, bridgeSessionId (e.g. 'session_01ABC...' when Remote Control is on), status, updatedAt. The same folder ALSO contains <pid>.<hex>.key files: NEVER open, read or stat anything except files named exactly /^\d{1,10}\.json$/. Transcripts (~/.claude/projects/<folder>/<sessionId>.jsonl) contain lines like {"type":"system","subtype":"bridge_status","url":"https://claude.ai/code/session_...","sessionId":...}.
Write tools/orchestrator-chat.mjs (ESM, SPDX header): `chatUrlFor(sessionId, { home = os.homedir(), transcriptPath = null, now = Date.now })` returns a URL string or null, never throws. 1) Scan ~/.claude/sessions for files matching /^\d{1,10}\.json$/ only (cap 500 files, 64 KB each), parse, pick the one whose sessionId === sessionId (prefer newest updatedAt), and if bridgeSessionId matches /^session_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,80}$/ return 'https://claude.ai/code/' + bridgeSessionId. 2) Else if transcriptPath is given and its real path is under ~/.claude/projects, read only its last 512 KB and take the newest bridge_status line's url. 3) Only ever return a string matching /^https:\/\/claude\.ai\/code\/session_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,80}$/ — anything else -> null. Cache the sessions-folder scan for 15 s (module-level, keyed by home). Tests tests/orchestrator-chat.test.mjs (temp home dirs): finds the URL by sessionId; ignores and never opens .key files (create one with mode 000 to prove it is never read); bad bridgeSessionId -> null; transcript fallback picks the newest bridge_status; a transcript outside <home>/.claude/projects is refused; a url on another host is refused; missing folders -> null. Run `node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/orchestrator-chat.test.mjs` and `node tools/check-package.mjs`.

TASK: a 'Capacity pools' view for Swarm Watch: for each capacity pool, its limit, how much is in use, whether it is capped and WHY. The MacBook seat will ship tools/pools.mjs later; no spec exists yet. Write the contract the board expects, an adapter that uses tools/pools.mjs when present, and a stub that derives pools from data already on disk. Read-only. Do NOT touch tools/swarm.mjs, tools/lanes.mjs or tools/spend.mjs.
1) docs/pools-board.md (short, plain words): the board calls `poolsSnapshot({ now })` exported by tools/pools.mjs when that file exists, expecting { pools: [ { id, name, kind: 'machine'|'project'|'lane'|'host'|'other', limit: number|null, inUse: number, unit: 'slots'|'usd'|'jobs', capped: boolean, why: string|null, until: ISO|null } ], at }. Until it exists the board shows a stub built from the lane store and config (list what). Related roadmap: R-022 (machine worker limit), R-032 (slots split across active projects by priority).
2) tools/pools-board.mjs: `async boardPools({ now = Date.now(), loadPools = defaultLoader, stub = stubPools, stubInput })`: defaultLoader dynamic-imports './pools.mjs' (relative to this module) and calls poolsSnapshot({ now }); if the file is missing or throws, use the stub; validate/clean every pool (numbers finite, strings <= 120 chars, kind in the list else 'other') and return { source: 'pools.mjs' | 'stub', pools, at }. Never throws.
   `stubPools({ workers, laneRows, hosts = [], now })` (pure): workers = workersHeld() output from tools/board-data.mjs ({ total, max, invalid, free, byProject? ... } — read it in context to use the real field names); laneRows = laneUsage() rows ({ lane, label, kind, todayUsd, dailyCapUsd, capResetsAt, limited:{state, until} }); hosts = config hosts [{ id, kind, capacity, enabled }]. Pools: one 'machine' pool (limit = max, inUse = total, unit 'slots', capped = max && total >= max, why = 'machine limit reached (N of N slots)' or 'limit invalid: fix machineConcurrency' when invalid); one 'project' pool per active project share if workersHeld exposes per-project holdings (limit = fair share = floor(max / active projects) as in docs: guaranteed share, borrowing idle capacity — say 'over its share, borrowing idle slots' when above share and others are idle); one 'lane' pool per lane row with a daily cap (unit 'usd', limit dailyCapUsd, inUse todayUsd, capped when todayUsd >= cap, why 'daily cap reached, resets <time>') or a pause (capped true, why 'rate limited until <time>' / 'quota paused until <time>', until); one 'host' pool per enabled remote host (unit 'jobs', limit capacity, inUse 0 unless known, why null).
3) tests/pools-board.test.mjs: stub math for machine full / not full / invalid, lane cap reached and pause, host pool; adapter uses an injected loader result when given, falls back to the stub when the loader throws or the module is missing, and cleans bad pool entries. Run `node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/pools-board.test.mjs` and `node tools/check-package.mjs`.
